paper.title: Near-linear Time Gaussian Process Optimization with Adaptive Batching and Resparsification

settings.name_in_paper: Batched GP optimization (frequentist, f in RKHS) with finite candidate set
unmapped: Batch sizes are chosen adaptively by the learner (batch terminated when 1 + sum of approximate posterior variances exceeds threshold C_tilde), not a fixed batch grid
settings.definition_quote: At each step $t$, the learner receives a feedback $y_t \triangleq f(\bx_t) + \eta_t$, where $f$ is an unknown function, and $\epsilon_t$ is an additive noise drawn i.i.d.\ from $\mathcal{N}(0,\xi^2)$. ... $R_T \triangleq \sum_{t=1}^T f^\star - f(\bx_t)$ ... we assume that $\armset$ is finite with cardinality $A$

symbols.Sig: sum_{t=1}^T sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t), sum of exact (rescaled) posterior variances at chosen points, approx gamma_T (log det(K_T/lambda + I))

conditions: noise N(0, xi^2), xi mapped to sigma_std
tuning: alpha_t = C_tilde * beta_t with beta_t = 2 xi sqrt(sum log(1+3 sigma~^2) + log(1/delta)) + (1+sqrt2) sqrt(lambda) F

source.label: thm:main-regret
source.quote: Assume $\normsmall{f}_{\rkhs} \leq F < \infty$, and let $\xi^2$ be the variance of the noise $\eta_t$. For any desired, $0 < \delta < 1$, $1 \leq \lambda$, $1 \leq \wt{C}$, if we run \bbkb with $\qbar_t \geq 72\wt{C}\log(4t/\delta)$, $\wt{\alpha}_{\fb{t}} = \wt{C}\wt{\beta}_{\fb{t}}$, and ... then, with prob. $1-\delta$, \bbkb's regret is bounded as $R_T^{\bbkb} \leq 55\wt{C}^2 R_T^{\bgpucb} \leq 55\wt{C}^3R_T^{\gpucb}$ with $R_T^{\gpucb}$ bounded by $\sqrt{T}(\xi(\sum\sigma_{t-1}^2(\bx_{t}) + \log(1/\delta)) + \sqrt{\lambda F^2\sum\sigma_{t-1}^2(\bx_{t})})$.

results.notes: Regret defined via function values f* - f(x_t), holds w.p. 1-delta. Bound is data-dependent via Sig ~ gamma_T (so O(sqrt(T) gamma_T)). The appendix proof's final line differs slightly in the placement of log(1/delta) (multiplying sqrt(lambda Sig)); recorded as stated in theorem. Companion Theorem 2 gives runtime O~(T A d_eff^2), dictionary size and number of batches O(d_eff) — computational, not recorded as regret.
